cohort: 249,257 female patients aged < 60 years who underwent breast cancer surgery between July 2010 and March 2020 in Japan
finding: While pregnant women undergoing breast cancer surgery were more likely to undergo total mastectomy and axillary dissection but less likely to undergo reconstruction, there were no significant differences in surgical outcomes between pregnant and non-pregnant women.
mod_finding: This study found that pregnant women undergoing breast cancer surgery were more likely to undergo total mastectomy and axillary dissection but less likely to undergo reconstruction compared to non-pregnant women, with 31 of 101 patients in the third trimester undergoing cesarean section.
